title: Ulyana and the Clock
premise: In the river town of Vellmora, on the eve of a revolution, Felix Montrose has spent ten years passing as her late father's apprentice in the print shop, hiding her identity behind the rhythms of type and ink. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the shop's ledger of names—records that could condemn half the townsfolk to conscription or worse—Felix discovers the ledger was never just a customer list: it is coded with the resistance's network. As soldiers occupy the workshop and the clock above the door counts down to the requisition deadline, Felix must finish printing a final broadsheet that will expose the army's orders, choosing between the safety of invisibility and the belonging she never believed she could claim. The book ends with the presses running as the clock strikes, the truth loose in the streets, and Felix stepping out from behind her father's name into her own.
about_author: Dominic Brightwater is the pen name of a former letterpress printer who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century press equipment in small-town museums. Their fiction draws on family stories of border towns caught between armies, and on a lifelong fascination with the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Letters
chapters.summary: Felix Montrose, working in her late father's print shop under his name, sorts type for a routine job while memorizing which neighbors' names appear in the ledger—and which must never be spoken aloud. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the quiet discipline of a life built on concealment, and the ache beneath it.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Felix's mentor, old Sera Ilyen, comes after hours to check the ledger, and Felix notices for the first time that certain entries carry tiny marks in the margins. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dawning curiosity mixed with fear—the ledger may hold more than accounts.

chapters.title: Drums on the River Road
chapters.summary: Word arrives that the Fourth Regiment is marching on Vellmora; the market empties by noon and Felix watches a boy she grew up with pack his family's cart. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the fragile normalcy of a town cracking open.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Officers arrive with papers claiming the town, its grain, and 'all records of population'; a captain named Aldous Verren posts notice that the ledger must be surrendered within nine days. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: cold dread—the ledger cannot be surrendered.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Sera reveals the margin marks are a cipher naming the resistance network; burning the ledger would doom them all to suspicion, but keeping it means finishing what it was meant to do. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the weight of inherited duty she never agreed to carry.

chapters.title: The Captain's Ink
chapters.summary: Verren visits the shop to commission official proclamations, and Felix, printing them, realizes he suspects nothing about her—or pretends not to; their conversation over type cases crackles with mutual recognition. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: dangerous fascination across enemy lines.

chapters.title: Marks in the Margin
chapters.summary: Felix deciphers the first page of the cipher alone at night and finds her own father's initials among the network's founders. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal braided together—the man who taught her silence was part of something loud.

chapters.title: The Clock Above the Door
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: ten years earlier, young Felix learns the trade while her father winds the shop clock each night, telling her the town runs on time kept by ordinary hands. POV: Felix (past). Emotional beat: tenderness, and the origin of everything she now questions.

chapters.title: Occupied Hours
chapters.summary: Soldiers billet in the square; a young private, Tam, lingers at the shop window asking honest questions about printing, and Felix sees the war through eyes younger than her own. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion complicating her anger.

chapters.title: Day Four: The Broadsheet
chapters.summary: Sera proposes the plan—print a broadsheet exposing the army's secret conscription orders before the deadline—but the type must be set in secret and the paper smuggled past checkpoints. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: terror hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Verren's Doubt
chapters.summary: Verren returns to proof the proclamations and lets slip, over a shared pot of coffee, that he has read the orders he is enforcing and does not believe in them. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: love against duty taking root where it should not.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Soldiers search neighboring shops for seditious material; Felix hides the cipher pages inside a forme of locked-up type, and the searchers pass inches from it. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: near-ruin, and the discovery that she can act under pressure.

chapters.title: Tam's Question
chapters.summary: Private Tam returns alone and asks Felix whether the proclamations are true; unable to lie to him outright, she sets him one line of type himself and watches him understand what words can cost. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: an unlikely alliance seeded in ink.

chapters.title: Day Six: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Sera is detained for questioning; Felix must decide whether to abandon the plan or finish it without her teacher, using only the fragments of cipher she has learned. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: isolation, then the choice to belong to the network even if it kills her.

chapters.title: Setting the Truth
chapters.summary: Working nights, Felix composes the broadsheet by hand, each word chosen to survive scrutiny; Verren nearly catches her at 3 a.m., and instead of reporting her, he corrects her kerning and leaves. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: love expressed as complicity, wordless and irreversible.

chapters.title: Day Seven: The Broken Forme
chapters.summary: A soldier's carelessness smashes a case of type and with it half the composed broadsheet; Felix must reset it in hours while the town's remaining resisters argue over whether to flee instead. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: despair met with stubborn craft.

chapters.title: The Deadline Moves
chapters.summary: Verren announces the ledger surrender has been moved up two days; Felix realizes someone informed, and every suspect face in the market becomes a question. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: paranoia fracturing the community she is trying to save.

chapters.title: Day Eight: Press Night
chapters.summary: With Tam standing watch and the clock ticking toward the morning inspection, Felix locks the final forme and begins the run; the press shakes the whole building as soldiers pound at the shutters. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: climax—the work finished at the exact moment discovery arrives.

chapters.title: The Clock Strikes
chapters.summary: Verren bursts in, finds the wet broadsheets, and reads the exposed orders; rather than arrest her, he pockets one copy and reports the press broken, buying the town its morning. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: sacrifice answered with sacrifice; love choosing duty to people over duty to uniform.

chapters.title: Paper in Every Doorway
chapters.summary: By dawn the broadsheet is in every doorway in Vellmora; the regiment's own soldiers read it, murmurs become refusal, and the conscription order collapses in the square. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by exhaustion and loss.

chapters.title: After the Reckoning
chapters.summary: Sera returns; the ledger's cipher is decoded fully and the network's survivors gather in the shop, asking Felix—not her father's ghost—to lead the rebuilding. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief honored, belonging finally claimed.

chapters.title: Felix Montrose, Printer
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Felix carves her own name into a new brass plate for the door, winds the clock herself, and opens the shop under a sign that bears no one's name but hers. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: resolution—identity no longer hidden, time now kept by her own hand.
